subject: Proposal: Zone-Based Geo Multipliers & Leveling Exception Process
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: Zone-Based Geo Multipliers & Leveling Exception Process

Team —

Attached is a first-pass proposal to move our geo adjustments from a static country table to a Zone-based multiplier model (geo_zone_matrix_v1.xlsx). The goal is to simplify offer math, reduce edge-case manual approvals, and make benchmarking easier across month-to-month fluctuation in local markets. Key points up front: 

- Zone model: three zones (Anchor, Mid, Outlier) with multipliers applied to US base bands. Multipliers are expressed as percentages (e.g., Zone Mid = 0.85–0.95).
- Leveling exceptions: propose a lightweight "Level Exception Form" (attached) for manager escalation when market or role rationale exists.
- Pilot: run a 6-week pilot in LATAM (Mexico/Colombia) and DACH SME markets to validate candidate experience and offer acceptance.

Please review the matrix and the example offer calculations (example-offer-calc.pdf). Ask for feedback on: 1) zone cutpoints, 2) exception thresholds (what counts as an exception vs routine override), and 3) telemetry we should capture during the pilot.

Action requested: everyone reply with one clear redline or question by EOD Friday so we can lock the pilot charter and vendor scope.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Comp & Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: geo_zone_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), example-offer-calc.pdf (sample calculations), level-exception-form.docx (draft)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Zone-Based Geo Multipliers & Leveling Exception Process

Appreciate the clear layout, Soojin. Quick notes from GTM hiring perspective: 

- Pilot markets: agree with LATAM + DACH. Two reasons: (1) clear ADP/benchmarks available, (2) we’ll see both high-variability (LATAM) and high-cost (DACH) signals.
- Zone communication: we must include recruiter-facing scripts so offers sound consistent (e.g., "we anchor to US band X and apply a regional adjustment"). I can draft the script.
- Exception owners: suggest routing exceptions to hiring manager + local HR lead + Comp within 48 hours.

Can we add Karthik and Marcus to the working group? Marcus for ops impacts (offer tool), Karthik for APAC parity considerations later.

Marissa
VP, GTM Recruiting

On attachments: please add a short recruiter FAQ page before pilot kickoff.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Zone-Based Geo Multipliers & Leveling Exception Process

LGTM overall. A few benchmarking notes: 

- I'll loop in Carl from CompBench for a 30-min calibration call (external) to sanity-check zone multipliers against our target percentiles (50/60/75).
- For LATAM we should be careful with total cash vs OTE framing; comp surveys there tend to undercount benefits. I'll ask Javier (local vendor) to share local MID-market comps.
- Exception threshold suggestion: any offer > 12% above the zone-adjusted amount should require a Level Exception Form + VP approval. Under 12% can be approved by Hiring Manager + Local HR.

I'll schedule the calibration call for next week and add proposed telemetry fields to the Drive doc.

Neha
Head of Comp Strategy

External: Carl D'Souza <carl@compbench.co>, Javier Morales <javier@latambench.com>

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Zone-Based Geo Multipliers & Leveling Exception Process

Quick calc checks after running sample heads against the matrix: 

- Example SR IC (US band 3): US midpoint $140k. Zone Mid multiplier 0.90 => local anchor $126k. With benefits equivalency and local tax withholding, total on-payroll cost is ~1.12x domestic cash.
- Manager (+1 band): Manager premium currently set at +18% over IC midpoint. With zone multiplier logic we preserve the premium but apply it after the multiplier (i.e., (US_mid * manager_premium) * zone_multiplier) — keeps promo ladders consistent.
- Offer toolkit impact: will need two new fields in Offer Builder: zone_code and exception_flag. Marcus can scope the UI change.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcGeoZoneProposal — I've dropped a sample CSV of 50 historical offers for modelling.

Aditya
Director, Talent Systems

Attachment: sample-offer-export-50.csv (in Drive)

Thanks all — consolidating next steps below (will post a one-pager to Notion later):

1) Pilot charter: LATAM + DACH, 6 weeks, targeted roles: SDR, SWE (IC L2-L4), and AM (GTM mid). Owner: Neha.
2) Vendor calibration call: Neha to set up with Carl and Javier for 08/05.
3) Offer Builder changes: Marcus + Aditya will spec zone_code + exception_flag fields; aim for a pilot-ready build by 08/20.
4) Exception policy: threshold = 12% above zone-adjusted anchor -> requires Level Exception Form + VP approval. Comp to draft escalation SOP.
5) Recruiter materials: Marissa to draft scripting + FAQ by 08/09.

Please confirm owners and dates in reply. I uploaded the latest attachments to Drive and included a very short offer letter stub in the folder to test formatting.

Closing note: aim for the pilot to be transparent to candidates — language matters. Use the recruiter script and avoid "discount" phrasing.

Cheers,
Soojin
Head of Comp & Talent Operations
Redwood Inference
